back: a signal whose value varies continuously (like a microphone's voltage) rather than jumping between discrete levels.
hardware that samples a continuous voltage and converts it to a number the CPU can read. On the ESP32: analogRead().
the SI unit of electric current; how many electrons flow past a point per second. See Current, Ohm's law.
the Atmel (now Microchip) 8-bit microcontroller family used in the Arduino Uno (ATmega328P).
the number of symbol changes per second on a serial line; 9600 baud ≈ 9600 bits/s. The ESP32's default debug baud is 115200.
a reusable solderless board with rows of connected sockets for prototyping circuits quickly.
a momentary switch; connect it with a pull-up or pull-down so the pin reads a defined level when unpressed.
the ability of a component (a Capacitor) to store charge, measured in farads (F).
a passive component that stores energy in an electric field; used for decoupling (smoothing power) and timing.
the periodic square wave that paces a microcontroller; a 16 MHz AVR executes close to one instruction per clock tick.
the rate of electric charge flow, measured in amps (A). Flows through a circuit.
in the ESP32 track, an object that bundles a peripheral's state (a pin) with its behavior (on/off), keeping hardware details tidy.
the manufacturer's authoritative document describing a chip's pins, registers, electrical limits, and timing. The ultimate reference for any microcontroller.
cleaning up the noisy on/off chatter a physical button produces when pressed, giving one clean edge instead of many.
a capacitor placed near an IC to absorb supply-voltage spikes and keep the chip's power stable.
a signal with only discrete levels (HIGH/LOW, 1/0), as opposed to Analog signal.
the fraction of a PWM period the output is HIGH, expressed as a %; 50 % gives the LED half brightness (on average).
Espressif's dual-core, Wi-Fi/Bluetooth-enabled SoC; the basis of the ESP32 devkit boards and this hub's C/C++ and MicroPython tracks.
the common 0 V reference for a circuit; every rail, device, and signal refers back to ground. Shared ground between boards is mandatory.
a pin you can configure as digital input or output, e.g. to read a button or drive an LED. See Pin, Register.
a two-wire serial bus (SDA + SCL) for connecting sensors and small devices; used by many breakout boards.
a pin configured as an input with an internal resistor pulling it HIGH; reading LOW then means "pressed/active". Saves an external resistor.
a diode that emits light; needs a Resistor to limit current. Long leg = anode, short leg = cathode.
the voltage that counts as HIGH vs LOW. The ESP32 is 3.3 V logic and is not 5 V tolerant — feeding it 5 V can damage it.
hardware registers exposed as ordinary memory addresses; setting a "pin" is just writing to a register. Core to the Arduino-in-C track.
the diagram language used across these tutorials to draw flowcharts and sequence diagrams.
a self-contained computer-on-a-chip: CPU, RAM, flash, and I/O on one die.
a lean reimplementation of Python 3 that runs directly on microcontrollers with a live REPL.
the Rust mode that forgoes the standard library (no OS/heap) for bare-metal targets. Core concept of the embedded Rust tutorial.
individually addressable RGB LED chips chained on a single data wire; driven in MicroPython via the neopixel module.
a programming construct bundling data and the functions that act on it; in C++ it's how we wrap a sensor or a pin.
the SI unit of electrical resistance.
V = I × R: voltage = current × resistance. The single most-used equation in electronics. See Voltage, Current, Resistance.
a GPIO configured to drive a HIGH or LOW voltage, e.g. to light an LED.
a physical or logical I/O terminal on a chip or board.
a programming variable that holds a memory address instead of a value; essential for register-level access in AVR C and for bridging to hardware in Rust.
a resistor from a signal to VCC that holds the line HIGH when nothing drives it low.
rapidly toggling a pin HIGH/LOW with a controlled Duty cycle; an LED appears a dimmer brightness (or a motor turns slower) at lower duty.
an interactive prompt where each line runs instantly; MicroPython's signature workflow.
a tiny piece of memory, often one byte, that controls or reflects hardware; e.g. DDRB, PORTB on the AVR.
how strongly a component opposes current, measured in ohms (Ω).
a passive component that resists current, protecting an LED or setting a reference level. Typical LED series value: 220 Ω.
a systems language with compile-time memory safety (ownership); well-suited to no_std embedded dev.
a method of sending data one bit at a time over a wire; the "Serial Monitor" and 9600/115200 baud links.
a four-wire high-speed serial interface for external chips and displays.
an integrated circuit that puts CPU plus peripherals (Wi-Fi, timers, ADC) together, like the ESP32.
internal hardware that counts clock cycles; powers delays, PWM, and microsecond timing.
electrical "pressure" or potential difference between two points, measured in volts.
see NeoPixel / WS2812.
the wireless networking protocol built into the ESP32; used in the HTTP server tutorial to control an LED from a browser.
a resistor that holds a pin at a defined logic level (high/low) when nothing else drives it; essential for buttons and open-drain lines.
rapidly switching a pin between high and low, varying the duty cycle to fake an analog output (LED dimming, servo control).
a programmable pin that can be an input (read) or output (drive high/low); the fundamental way a microcontroller talks to the world.
a two-wire (SDA+SCL) serial bus for connecting sensors and displays; each device has an address.
a fast four-wire serial bus (MOSI/MISO/SCK/CS) used for SD cards, displays, and high-speed sensors.
an asynchronous two-wire serial link (TX/RX) used for debugging and GPS/module communication; configurable baud rate.
samples a continuous voltage and returns a number; on the ESP32 analogRead() returns 0–4095 (12-bit).
converts a number to an analog voltage; the ESP32 has 2 (8-bit) DAC channels.
an OS for microcontrollers that schedules tasks with priorities and guarantees timing; e.g. FreeRTOS on the ESP32.
a self-contained function scheduled by the RTOS; FreeRTOS runs the highest-priority ready task.
a lock that guarantees exclusive access to a shared resource between tasks.
a thread-safe buffer for passing data between tasks; FreeRTOS xQueueSend/xQueueReceive.
a counter used for signaling between tasks (binary = mutex-like, counting = resource counting).
a voltage-controlled transistor used to switch higher-power loads (motors, LEDs) from a microcontroller pin.
a current-controlled transistor; the classic amplifier and switch building block.
a high-gain differential amplifier; used for comparators, filters, and signal conditioning.
two resistors in series that produce a fraction of the input voltage; used to scale signals into ADC range.
a small capacitor (0.1 µF typical) placed near a chip's power pin to smooth supply noise.
an instrument that displays voltage vs time; essential for debugging signals, PWM, and serial.
a handheld meter that measures voltage, current, and resistance; the first tool every electronics learner needs.
a diode that emits light when forward-biased; needs a current-limiting resistor.
an addressable RGB LED with an integrated driver chip; many can be chained on one data pin.
a motor with position feedback controlled by a PWM pulse width (typically 1–2 ms at 50 Hz).
a transistor circuit that lets a motor spin both directions by reversing current flow.
code that runs when an interrupt fires; should be short and avoid blocking calls.
the practice of ignoring the mechanical bouncing of a switch contact (software delay or RC filter).
remapping a microcontroller pin's function (e.g. UART TX to a different pin).
built-in ROM code that loads user firmware over USB/serial; on the ESP32 held by GPIO0 during reset.
non-volatile storage for firmware; on the ESP32 also stores filesystem (SPIFFS/LittleFS).
a timer that resets the MCU if the firmware stops responding; guards against hangs.
triggering code on a pin edge (rising/falling); used for buttons and sensors without polling.
a board with copper traces connecting components; designed in KiCad/EasyEDA then fabricated.
the symbolic circuit diagram showing how components connect; the first step of any PCB design.
the physical pad layout on a board that a component solders onto; chosen per component in the EDA tool.
the standard format (RS-274X) that describes each copper/solder-mask layer for PCB fabrication.
a plated hole connecting copper layers of a PCB; used to route signals between layers.
melting solder paste in an oven/plate to attach SMD components to a board.
a low-melting-point metal alloy that joins components to the board; lead-free (Sn-Ag-Cu) is standard.
a portable DC power source; Li-ion/LiPo cells need charge-protection circuits (do not over-discharge).
a component that outputs a fixed voltage (e.g. 5V, 3.3V) from a higher/unstable input; linear (LDO) or switching (buck/boost).
a switching regulator that steps voltage down efficiently; the ESP32 dev boards use one to derive 3.3V.
the 0V reference node; everything in a circuit is measured relative to it. Star grounding avoids loops.
unwanted voltage fluctuations on signals; reduced by decoupling, shielding, and proper grounding.
a low-power wireless protocol on the ESP32; used for beacons, sensors, and phone apps.
a lightweight publish/subscribe message protocol for IoT over Wi-Fi; the ESP32 talks to brokers like Mosquitto.
running a web server on the ESP32 to serve pages/control GPIO from a browser.
filesystems for the ESP32 flash; store config, web assets, and data that survives reboot.
running small machine-learning models (TensorFlow Lite Micro) on microcontrollers like the ESP32/STM32.
hardware debugging interfaces to step code, set breakpoints, and flash MCUs (ST-Link, J-Link).
an instrument that captures digital signals over time; invaluable for debugging I²C/SPI/UART.
implementing a protocol in code (toggling pins manually) when no hardware peripheral is available.
the built-in TWDT (Task Watchdog) resets the chip if a task hangs; enable it in long-running projects.
an ultra-low-power mode where the CPU is off and only RTC + ULP run; wake by timer or GPIO.
Espressif's connectionless peer-to-peer protocol; low-latency, low-power communication between ESP32s without Wi-Fi infrastructure.
